title: Reading Drill — Studying bread orders at a canteen — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Studying bread orders at a canteen — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Elmbrook, work on unsold loaves taking up counter space at closing time had already produced a small collection of daily counts. The kitchen buyer used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: the weight of food left over.

**B** The group kept smaller late-afternoon orders for the new trial, which was planned to run for ten weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that changes in meal attendance should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
